units.source_text: 1. [\[19\]](../Text/chapter19.xhtml#fnref19) 日本纸牌，以日文字母排列，每张印有一首和歌，一人唱牌上的和歌，其他人抢该牌，先抢到者为优胜。​

en.t: Japanese playing cards arranged in the order of the Japanese syllabary; each card is printed with a waka poem. One person recites the poem on a card, and the others compete to take that card; the first to take it wins.
In Japanese, the term “hibo,” literally “sorrowful mother,” can also be understood to mean a loving mother.
